architectural-design.title: Architectural design
architectural-design.short: Villas, buildings and mosques drawn from the plot up. Plans that work for the family and the street.
architectural-design.hero: Plans that start with how you live
architectural-design.intro: We design from the plot and the brief: setbacks, sun, privacy and the way your family uses the house. Every plan is drawn to be approved and to be built.

process.title: Brief and site visit
process.text: We measure the plot and agree the room list.

process.title: Concept options
process.text: Two or three layouts to compare.

process.title: Developed design
process.text: One plan refined with elevations and 3D views.

process.title: Working drawings
process.text: The full set for approval and tender.

faq.q: How long does a villa design take?
faq.a: Concept design usually takes a few weeks. The full drawing set depends on the size of the villa and how quickly decisions are made.

faq.q: Can you design to my budget?
faq.a: Yes. We set a target area and specification at the start and check the design against it at each stage.

faq.q: Do you design traditional and contemporary styles?
faq.a: Both. Many of our villas mix contemporary lines with screens, courtyards and parapets from local architecture.

faq.q: Will the design be approved by the municipality?
faq.a: We design to RAK Municipality regulations from the first sketch, so the approval drawings follow directly from the design.

structural-engineering.title: Structural engineering
structural-engineering.short: Foundations, frames and slabs sized for the load and checked against UAE codes.
structural-engineering.hero: The part of the building you never see
structural-engineering.intro: We design the structure that carries the building: foundations for the soil on your plot, and a frame that is safe, economical and easy to build.

process.title: Soil and loads
process.text: We read the soil report and set the design loads.

process.title: Structural system
process.text: Grid, spans and materials agreed with the architect.

process.title: Analysis
process.text: Every element checked by calculation.

process.title: Drawings
process.text: Reinforcement details ready for site.

faq.q: Do I need a soil test?
faq.a: Yes. RAK Municipality requires a soil investigation, and the foundation design depends on it. We can arrange one.

faq.q: Can you check an existing structure?
faq.a: Yes. We assess existing buildings for extensions, additional floors or visible defects.

faq.q: Concrete or steel?
faq.a: Most villas and residential buildings are reinforced concrete. Steel suits warehouses and long spans. We recommend what fits the project.

faq.q: Who checks the structure on site?
faq.a: If you appoint us for supervision, our engineers inspect the reinforcement before each pour.

mep-design.title: MEP design
mep-design.short: Cooling, drainage, water and power routed through the building before the concrete is poured.
mep-design.intro: Mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems take space. We plan their routes together with the structure, so ducts and pipes fit without cutting beams on site.
deliverables: Load schedule for FEWA / RAK utilities

process.title: Loads
process.text: Cooling, power and water demand for every room.

process.title: Systems
process.text: Equipment and routes chosen with the architect.

process.title: Coordination
process.text: Ducts and pipes checked against the structure.

process.title: Drawings
process.text: Layouts and schedules for approval and tender.

faq.q: Do you design for Civil Defence approval?
faq.a: Yes. Fire fighting and fire alarm drawings are prepared to Civil Defence requirements.

faq.q: Can you reduce cooling costs?
faq.a: Shading, insulation and correctly sized equipment make the largest difference. We consider all three.

faq.q: Do you design solar or smart home systems?
faq.a: We can allow for them in the electrical design and coordinate with specialist suppliers.

faq.q: Is MEP design needed for a villa?
faq.a: Yes. MEP drawings are part of the municipality submission and the contractor prices from them.

construction-supervision.title: Construction supervision
construction-supervision.short: The engineer who drew it inspects it, from the first excavation to the final certificate.
construction-supervision.hero: On site until the keys are handed over
construction-supervision.intro: Supervision makes sure the building on site matches the drawings. We inspect key stages, approve materials and keep you informed.

process.title: Mobilisation
process.text: Setting-out checked before excavation.

process.title: Structure
process.text: Reinforcement inspected before every pour.

process.title: Finishes and services
process.text: Materials approved against the specification.

process.title: Handover
process.text: Snag list, completion certificate and keys.

faq.q: How often do you visit the site?
faq.a: At every key stage and on a regular schedule agreed in the contract.

faq.q: Do you work with any contractor?
faq.a: Yes. We can also help you compare tenders and choose one.

faq.q: Do I get reports?
faq.a: Yes, written reports with photos after inspections.

faq.q: Who issues the completion certificate?
faq.a: The municipality, after inspection. We prepare and submit the documents.

approvals-permits.title: Approvals and permits
approvals-permits.short: Drawings prepared, submitted and followed up with RAK Municipality and Civil Defence.
approvals-permits.hero: The right drawings, the first time
approvals-permits.intro: Approvals take time when drawings are returned for corrections. We prepare submissions to the current requirements and follow them through.

process.title: Check
process.text: Plot, zoning and requirements confirmed.

process.title: Prepare
process.text: Drawings and forms completed.

process.title: Submit
process.text: Applications lodged with each authority.

process.title: Follow up
process.text: Comments answered until approval.

faq.q: Can you get approval for drawings made by someone else?
faq.a: We can review them and resubmit under our name once they meet the requirements.

faq.q: How long does approval take?
faq.a: It depends on the authority and the project. Complete submissions are approved faster.

faq.q: Do I need a permit for an extension?
faq.a: Yes. Extensions and added floors need a permit and usually a structural check.

faq.q: Do you handle Civil Defence?
faq.a: Yes, as part of the same submission package.

interior-design.title: Interior design
interior-design.short: Room layouts, finishes and lighting, coordinated with every service behind the walls.
interior-design.hero: Rooms that are calm to live in
interior-design.intro: Interior design starts with the plan: where furniture stands, where light falls and where services run. We design interiors together with the building, not after it.

process.title: Brief
process.text: How each room is used and by whom.

process.title: Concept
process.text: Mood, materials and layout.

process.title: Details
process.text: Drawings for joinery, ceilings and lighting.

process.title: Site
process.text: Samples approved and installation checked.

faq.q: Do you design majlis interiors?
faq.a: Yes. Majlis, family living and private areas each have their own requirements, and we design them together.

faq.q: Can you design interiors for an existing villa?
faq.a: Yes. We survey the villa first and work with what is there.

faq.q: Do you supply furniture?
faq.a: We specify and coordinate with suppliers you choose.

faq.q: Will lighting be coordinated with the ceiling?
faq.a: Yes. Lighting, cooling and ceiling design are drawn together.

villa-al-dhait.title: Courtyard villa, Al Dhait
villa-al-dhait.brief: A family villa around a shaded courtyard, with a separate majlis for guests and private rooms upstairs.
villa-al-dhait.solution: Two wings linked by a covered walkway, deep parapets and screen walls on the street side, and a structure planned around the courtyard spans.

residential-al-nakheel.title: Residential building, Al Nakheel
residential-al-nakheel.brief: Apartments on a narrow plot with parking at ground level.
residential-al-nakheel.solution: A transfer slab over the parking, stacked services cores and balconies shaded by the floor above.

mosque-khuzam.title: Neighbourhood mosque, Khuzam
mosque-khuzam.brief: A mosque for a residential district, with ablution areas and a women's prayer hall.
mosque-khuzam.solution: A clear-span prayer hall under a concrete dome, with quiet cooling designed around prayer times.

warehouse-al-ghail.title: Warehouse, Al Ghail
warehouse-al-ghail.location: Al Ghail Industrial Area, Ras Al Khaimah
warehouse-al-ghail.brief: A storage warehouse with offices and loading bays.
warehouse-al-ghail.solution: A steel portal frame on pad foundations, with a mezzanine office and fire fighting to Civil Defence requirements.

villa-julan.title: Contemporary villa, Julan
villa-julan.brief: A two-storey villa with a large family living area and views to the mountains.
villa-julan.solution: A double-height living room facing the view, shaded glazing and interiors designed with the house.

commercial-al-hisn.title: Commercial building, Al Hisn
commercial-al-hisn.brief: Shops at street level with offices above.
commercial-al-hisn.solution: An open retail floor, flexible office floors and a services strategy that lets each tenant fit out separately.

residential-dafan.title: Residential building, Dafan Al Nakheel
residential-dafan.location: Dafan Al Nakheel, Ras Al Khaimah
residential-dafan.brief: A six-storey residential building on a corner plot.
residential-dafan.solution: A regular column grid for economy and fast construction, supervised stage by stage.

villa-mina-al-arab.title: Villa, Mina Al Arab
villa-mina-al-arab.location: Mina Al Arab, Ras Al Khaimah
villa-mina-al-arab.brief: A villa close to the water, with interiors designed at the same time as the building.
villa-mina-al-arab.solution: Rooms arranged for sea breezes, materials chosen for the coastal climate and interiors coordinated with services.
